### Added

- **Files is experimental, off until switched on**: Settings › General › Experimental › Files turns on the Pages tab, a note as a page and everything built on it (editing, blocks, properties, managing files, changes from outside merged in, live co-editing, history, comments, mentions and the Inbox). Off, which is the default for everyone, Relay is as before: the sidebar has no tabs and a note opens in the side panel. The switch for making a team workspace's notes documents shows only with Files on; a workspace that already has documents keeps syncing them either way (#331)
- **Mentions and an Inbox for comments**: in a comment or reply on a team workspace's page, @ lists the other members by what you type, and the one you pick is mentioned. A member who is mentioned gets a banner once (and a push without text on a paired phone), also when the comment came while they were offline. The workspace menu of a team workspace gets an Inbox with its open threads that mention you or are on a page you edited; a click opens the page on that thread, and resolving it takes it out. Author names in a page's history now show for every member, not as hex (#330)
- **Comments on a page**: the speech bubble in a page's bar opens its comments beside it (in the history's place, one at a time). Select text and click Comment, or press ⌥⌘M, to start a thread; reply, resolve, reopen, and delete what you wrote. The commented text is marked in the page and a click on it opens its thread; resolved threads fold away under Resolved. On a shared workspace's document the comments sync to every member, live, each shown under the name of the member who really wrote it, and they stay on their words while anyone edits around them; on any other note they stay on this Mac. Comments never change the note's file. Agents get `relay comments.list` and `relay comments.reply` (asks first) for their own workspace's pages (#329)
- **A page's history**: the clock in a page's bar opens its versions beside it, newest first: who made each, when, and what made it (Claude, on disk, restored), with the lines added and removed. Pick one to see what changed since, and Restore makes it the page's text again. In a shared workspace a note that is a document has every editing session from its log (history is kept for good), and a restore is an edit like any other, so every member gets it and it shows in the history itself. Any other note shows the commits of its workspace's git repo that changed it, also across a rename; a workspace that is no git repo has no history (#328)
- **Edit a shared page together**: a page whose note is a document of a shared workspace is edited live with the other members on it. What they type shows as they type it, their cursors and selections show with their names, and their avatars sit in the page's bar. What is typed here goes straight into the document, which writes the file, and ⌘Z undoes only your own typing. A change Claude or Obsidian makes to the file lands in the open page too (#327)
- **A page merges changes made outside Relay**: when Claude, Obsidian, git or a shared round changes the file of a page you have open, the change lands in the editor while you keep typing, as long as you did not change the same lines; the changed lines are marked "Updated by Claude" or "Updated on disk" for a moment, and ⌘Z does not undo them. Changes on the same lines show the Reload / Keep mine bar as before. Relay now watches the workspace folders for this, so the Pages tab also shows a new, renamed or removed note right away instead of within 30 seconds (#305)
- **Manage pages and folders in the Pages tab**: right-click a page or folder for New page, New folder, Rename…, Move to…, Duplicate, Reveal in Finder, Copy path and Delete, or drag a page or folder onto a folder to move it there. A rename or move rewrites the links to it across the workspace ([[Name]], [[Name|alias]], [[folder/Name]], [[Name#heading]], embeds and markdown links), keeping each link's form, and first says how many ("Update 3 links in 2 notes"); a name two notes share is left alone. A note changed after the count stops the move, and a stopped or failed move puts back what it wrote, naming anything it could not. Delete asks first and moves it into the workspace's .trash/ with Undo; in a shared workspace it says it deletes for every member. A project's own note keeps its name: rename the project from the sidebar. In a shared workspace a move's old files pass the sync's delete brake for one round, as server deletes of the content they had; a delete is braked like any other. The page view also shows the bottom bar now (Undo, errors), which it left out before (#304)
- **Edit a page's properties in its header**: each frontmatter key is a row to edit, by what its value is: text (offering the values the key already has in the workspace's notes), a date picker, a list as chips with an × each and a box to add one, a [[note]] link with an arrow to open it, or a checkbox. Remove a key with its ×, drag its name to move it, add one at the bottom with a name and a type. Only the edited key's lines change in the file: comments, quoting and keys Relay does not know stay as they were, and a hand-written line YAML refuses (an unquoted `:` in a description) stays editable as text (#303)
- **Notion-like editing on a page**: type / on an empty line for a menu of blocks (headings, to-do, bulleted and numbered list, quote, callout, code, table, divider, link to page) that puts their markdown there; [[ completes the workspace's note names; the handle left of a block drags it elsewhere (a heading takes its section along, a list item its nested items) and opens Turn into, Duplicate and Delete, plus Add row and Add column on a table; Tab and Shift-Tab move between a table's cells and Tab in the last one adds a row; a URL pasted over selected text makes it a link. The file stays plain markdown (#302)
- **Shared workspaces' notes as documents, when an admin turns it on**: Settings › Machines has a switch per shared workspace, off by default, which an admin turns on for every member. Then an admin's Relay turns the workspace's notes into documents a few at a time, so members' edits to them merge instead of making conflict copies. A change to such a note's file (Claude, Obsidian, a page's save, git) goes into its document as the part that changed, on top of what others changed meanwhile, never as the whole file over it, and says who made it. A note moved in the Pages tab keeps its document; one deleted there goes from every Mac and comes back with Undo; a note's file deleted any other way is written back. An older Relay keeps syncing the other files and gets "update Relay" for a note that is a document now (#326)
- **Documents in shared workspaces, underneath**: a note several members edit can now be a document that merges their edits instead of a file copied whole. The relay-server keeps per document an append-only log of updates sealed on the members' Macs, plus snapshots, and never deletes them (the history to come); a pushed edit reaches the other members over the live channel at once, and every round pulls what is missing and writes the note. A note keeps its document when it is renamed. Nothing makes a note a document yet: that comes with turning existing notes into documents and the editor (#325)
- **A workspace's key changes when someone leaves**: removing a member, a member leaving or `relay-server revoke` makes an admin's Relay rotate the workspace key on its next round. The new key goes to every member left, sealed to each one's own public key, and the server refuses writes under the old one, so what is written after does not open with what the removed member holds. Who is in a workspace and which key is current now come from a signed member list that every Mac checks from the workspace's creator, so the server cannot hand out a key of its own, add or promote anyone, or hide a removal; holding entries back is noticed, also from other members' files. A new workspace starts its list at once; an existing one gets it from its first admin on this version. Settings › Machines warns about a member list it cannot trust, and an admin can trust a member's new keys after they set up Relay again. Old files keep their key; an invite carries every key, so a new member reads all of it. Needs the relay-server of this release (#322)
- **A live channel for shared workspaces**: next to the sync every 10 s, Relay keeps a connection to the workspace's server open, over which members' changes will reach each other within moments (the documents edited together come next; this is the channel). The frames are sealed on each Mac like the files, and the server passes them on without keeping them. The workspace menu says per team workspace whether it is live or syncing every 10 s. A removed member's channel closes at once. Needs the server updated to this release; an older one keeps working with rounds only (#321)
- **A moved project takes its conversations along**: Move to workspace now moves the project's Claude Code conversations too, with their transcripts, so they show under the project in the new workspace and continue there. One that ran with Codex or OpenCode, or that read mail when the target is a team workspace, stays behind as a general conversation, and the dialog says which and why. Into a team workspace the dialog also lists the conversations under the same tick. The move waits while one of them is working, waiting on you, on a work machine or shared with the phone. Copy leaves conversations where they are (#299)

- **Move or copy a project to another workspace**: right-click a project, Move to workspace or Copy to workspace. Its notes (the project's folder), its work-state row (or its card, in a workspace that builds its work-state from cards), its icon, Design link, linked repos and scratch notes go along. Nothing is written when something of that name is already there, and a move removes only what was copied, once every write worked. Into a team workspace the files are listed and Move waits until you tick that every member may see them; files a team workspace does not sync stay behind. Conversations that already started stay in the workspace they ran in, as general conversations there (#296)

### Changed

- **Edit a page**: a page in the middle column is now an editor. The markdown stays as it is in the file, shown as Obsidian does: headings, bold and italic, links and [[links]], lists, to-dos (tick one to change the file), quotes and callouts look formatted, and the line you are on shows its markdown. A [[link]] opens its page, ⌘-click opens it in the right drawer. What you type is saved a second after you stop, when you leave the page and with ⌘S; the frontmatter and the title line stay untouched. When the note changed on disk since you opened it, nothing is written and a bar offers Reload or Keep mine. A note over 1 MB stays read-only. In a team workspace the change goes out with its next round, as a change made in Obsidian does (#301)
- **A page opens in the middle**: a note picked in the Pages tab now opens as a page in the middle column instead of the right drawer: its folders, icon and title, its properties, for a project's note how many conversations it has and the time of the latest, then the note itself. The bar shows when the note was last edited and Ask Claude, which starts a conversation in the note's workspace with its path typed in. Notes opened from a conversation still open in the drawer (#300)
- **Chats and Pages in the sidebar**: two tabs under the search, each with its count; ⌘. swaps them (Settings › Shortcuts). Pages lists the notes of the workspace shown: Recent (the notes your conversations read and wrote this week), then per context its projects with their note counts (a project unfolds to its folder), then every folder of the workspace. The search finds notes by name, and a note opens in the right drawer (#298)
- **One workspace at a time, picked in the sidebar's footer**: your own vault is now your Personal workspace, next to the vault folders you added and the shared workspaces. The footer shows the workspace with its note count; click it for the list of workspaces (⌃1 to ⌃9 switch too, changeable in Settings › Shortcuts), Open a folder as workspace…, New workspace from template… and Workspace settings. The sidebar's projects, general conversations and search follow the workspace shown, and a new general conversation you start there runs in it (one from a reminder, a ticket or the Brain stays in Personal). A conversation that ran in a folder since removed shows under Personal with that folder's name. Reminders, mail and Today stay on your Personal workspace. Usage, light/dark and Settings moved from the footer into that menu; a usage warning or a Relay update puts a dot on the workspace's square. The app now says workspace where it said vault for these folders (#294)
